title: IND-CCA Security Versus Circular Security
summary: An IND-CCA-secure but non-circular-secure system is generically attainable, but it remains unresolved whether IND-CCA offers greater resistance to circular-security attacks than IND-CPA.

formal_statement.body: For private-key bit-encryption systems, determine whether replacing $\text{IND-CPA}$ security with chosen-ciphertext ($\text{IND-CCA}$) security makes circular-security attacks less effective or makes circular security more likely. The relevant separation setting permits an $\text{IND-CCA}$-secure bit-encryption system that is not circular secure, and such a system can be obtained generically by combining an $\text{IND-CPA}$-secure but not circular-secure bit-encryption system with a multi-bit CCA-secure encryption scheme. The unresolved task is to determine whether $\text{IND-CCA}$ security nevertheless provides greater resistance to circular-security attacks than $\text{IND-CPA}$ security.

scope.domain: Private-key bit-encryption security, comparing chosen-ciphertext security with circular-security resistance.
parameters: IND-CPA and IND-CCA security as the compared security notions
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether IND-CCA security provides greater resistance to circular-security attacks than IND-CPA security.

citations.label: Separating Semantic and Circular Security for Symmetric-Key Bit Encryption from the Learning with Errors Assumption

progress.summary: The source explicitly poses whether chosen-ciphertext security makes a bit-encryption system more resistant to circular-security attacks. It also presents a generic IND-CCA-secure but non-circular-secure separation, leaving the comparative resistance question open.
